abstract: The Indian population, characterized by extensive ethnolinguistic and biogeographical diversity, is significantly underrepresented in global genomic resources limiting the development of genomic medicine in South Asia. To address this, ~10 000 genomes from 83 populations were sequenced as part of the GenomeIndia initiative (Department of Biotechnology, Government of India). Here, we present GI-DB (accessible at https://ibdc.dbt.gov.in/gidb/), a public resource cataloging 136 million high-confidence variants, including 44 million variants which are not present in other global and South Asian databases. GI-DB serves as a population-specific reference resource for genetic variation across Indian populations. It can support the interpretation of clinically relevant variations for rare disease, complex disorders, and pharmacogenomics. The database is structured to provide allele frequency stratification across tribal and non-tribal groups, biogeography, and ethnolinguistic categories. The interactive browser facilitates exploration of variants and genes of interest, offering detailed annotations from tools like VEP, ClinVar, and comparisons with global databases like 1000 Genomes, gnomAD, and GenomeAsia. Researchers can search using different modalities and access data programmatically. GI-DB is a foundational resource for genomics-informed public health and clinical genetics, tailored for the Indian population.
